ATC Vet — QC02DB01. (dihydralazine) Pharmacopoeias. In Chin. and Eur. (see p.vii). Ph. Eur. 6.2 (Dihydralazine Sulphate, Hydrated). A white or slightly yellow crystalline powder. Slightly soluble in water; practically insoluble in dehydrated alcohol. It dissolves in dilute mineral acids. Profile Dihydralazine is a vasodilator with actions and uses similar to those of hydralazine (p.1305). It is given orally as the sulfate. Dihydralazine sulfate hemipentahydrate 14.45 mg is equivalent to about 12.5 mg of anhydrous dihydralazine sulfate. In hyper- tension (p.1171) the usual initial dose is the equivalent of 12.5 mg of anhydrous dihydralazine sulfate twice daily and the maximum recommended dose is 50 mg twice daily. Higher dos- es have been used in the management of heart failure. Other salts of dihydralazine that have been used in oral prepara- tions include the hydrochloride and the tartrate.
